propositions: A failed identity write (add_label or set_entity_property) after successful Jira issue creation triggers delete_issue, destroying a recoverable unlabelled issue
The write-ahead binding (record_pending_key) is persisted before identity writes, leaving a keyed-pending entry pointing to a deleted Jira key that recover_pending cannot resolve
recover_pending's keyed branch exists to retro-attach identity markers deterministically without search, making the rollback delete redundant with existing recovery machinery

Jira rejects field writes with misleading screen-not-found messages in at least three distinct situations: missing Create/Edit screen configuration, jira.permission.createclone.denied workflow property, or malformed field values

Removing the delete and leaving the binding keyed-pending allows recover_pending to complete the operation on retry, while a BindingPersistError (where no key was recorded) safely produces an unmarked issue adopted as new remote on next inbound pass

The issue survives and binding remains recoverable only if a subsequent recover_pending pass can succeed, whereas permanent failures will re-attempt and fail on every pass, requiring operator intervention regardless of approach
